title: Lesson 9: Fighting for Purity
description: Purity is not how you earn God's love. It is how you protect a heart that already belongs to Him. Through King David's fall, Jesus' words about the heart, and 1 Corinthians 6, you will learn what to do when temptation fires the starting gun: RUN. Remember the Cross, United with God, and Need others.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you saw that God keeps covenant with you first, and that as two people draw near to God, they draw near to each other. This lesson turns to purity, which means guarding your body, your eyes, and your mind. Purity keeps your closest relationships faithful and your heart free. Purity matters whether you are married or single, and it always starts with grace.

blocks.alt: King David, fully clothed, alone on his palace roof overlooking the city, with his royal robe and crown set aside

blocks.title: The View from the Roof
blocks.text:
David was Israel's greatest king, a man the Bible describes as a man after God's own heart (1 Samuel 13:14). One spring, at the time when kings usually went out to battle, David stayed home in Jerusalem while his army went to war (2 Samuel 11:1).

Late one afternoon, he got up from his couch and walked on the roof of his palace. From there he saw a woman bathing. Instead of turning away, David pursued what he saw. He sent someone to find out who she was and learned that she was Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah, one of his own soldiers. Then David used his power as king. He "sent messengers and took her" (2 Samuel 11:4).

When Bathsheba became pregnant, David tried to hide what he had done. When hiding failed, he arranged for Uriah to be killed in battle. One look became a string of choices, and each one made the next one easier. The chapter ends with one heavy sentence: "But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD" (2 Samuel 11:27).

David kept his sin hidden until God sent the prophet Nathan to confront him. Then David finally said, "I have sinned against the LORD." Nathan answered with words David did not deserve: "The LORD also has put away your sin" (2 Samuel 12:13).

David's story is a warning, but it is also a rescue. Years before, a young man named Joseph faced a similar temptation in Egypt, and he ran. The Bible says "he left his garment in her hand and fled" (Genesis 39:12). David did not run. He stayed on the roof, and one look became a string of choices. Sin still works that way. The enemy uses temptation to steal your peace, kill your closest relationships, and destroy your life. But Jesus came to give life.
The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I came that they may have life and have it abundantly.

Before you read a single strategy in this lesson, hold on to that. Jesus did not just die to forgive you of all the sin you have done and will do. He died to give you the power to fight sin, and to build your life on His direction instead of your desires.
9.1 - Consider David's story: a look, the wrong decision, hiding his sin, and a long silence. Why do you think the first steps matter so much when it comes to temptation?
The RUN Plan
Paul wrote 1 Corinthians to young Christians in Corinth, a city full of sexual temptation. Read the heart of what he told them, and notice the words in bold. They are the RUN plan.

But he who is joined to the Lord becomes one spirit with him. Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against his own body. Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body.

Flee means run. Picture a race. When temptation fires the starting gun, you have a split second to choose: run toward life, or stay and slide toward the pit. Do not negotiate, and do not see how close you can get. Close the app, turn off the show, leave the room, or put a filter on your phone. Paul gives three reasons you can run and keep running. Together they spell RUN. Try it below.

R is for Remember the Cross. Temptation tells you that your body is yours to use however you want. Paul says the opposite: you are not your own, because you were bought with a price, and that price was paid at the cross. You were bought with the life of Jesus. You are not fighting for purity so God will let you into His family. You are fighting because you are already in it. God is not a boss waiting on your performance. He is a Father who paid everything for you, and He wants you free.
9.2 - Has your fight for purity mostly been driven by fear of getting caught or by love for a Father who already calls you His own? What might change if love became the reason?

U is for United with God. Look at how much of God this passage puts inside you. You are joined to the Lord and one spirit with him. Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you. And you are called to glorify God the Father in your body. Father, Son, and Spirit are all in this with you, so you never run in your own strength.

I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.

So you run from sin, and you run to Jesus. He understands temptation from the inside, because He was "tempted as we are, yet without sin" (Hebrews 4:15). Running to Him can be as simple as whispering, "Lord Jesus, I need Your grace right now. Be my strength." And He is the better joy. In His presence "there is fullness of joy" (Psalm 16:11), the joy temptation promises and never delivers.

N is for Need others. Paul told young Timothy to run, but not alone. Notice all the 2s in the reference, 2 Timothy 2:22. Let them remind you that you need at least two trusted believers running with you.
So flee youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, along with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.

Sin grows best in hiding, just as it did for David. Not everything private is sinful, and you do not need to tell everyone everything. But a struggle you hide from everyone who could help you tends to grow in the dark. James says, "confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed" (James 5:16). God gives you brothers and sisters in Christ so that you do not have to run alone.
When the Thought Knocks
Purity is not only about what you do. In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus took it all the way to the heart.
You have heard that it was said, 'You shall not commit adultery.' But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

Jesus is not saying every passing thought is a sin. He was tempted Himself, yet without sin. A tempting thought is a knock at the door. Lust is opening the door, inviting the thought in, and letting it stay (James 1:14-15). That is why Jesus used such strong words about cutting off whatever leads you into sin (Matthew 5:29-30). He was not asking you to hurt yourself. He was telling you to take drastic, practical action.
Long before Jesus preached this, Job made a decision ahead of time about what he would do with his eyes. He made it a covenant, a promise he meant to keep even when.
I made a covenant with my eyes not to look lustfully at a young woman.

So when the thought knocks, run. Paul says to "take every thought captive to obey Christ" (2 Corinthians 10:5). Name the thought, hand it to Jesus, and choose what is good instead. And do not believe the lies. Jesus called the devil a liar (John 8:44), and temptation always lies: "No one will know." "It won't hurt anyone." "You deserve this." "You're too far gone." Answer every lie with the truth: Christ bought you at the cross, God Himself lives in you, and you are not alone.
9.3 - What is one habit or boundary you can establish to better protect your mind and heart?
When You Have Already Fallen

Maybe you read David's story and thought, "That is me." If so, the most important part of his story is not the fall. It is what happened when he stopped hiding. God did not throw David away. He forgave him, and He will forgive you.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

Confession opens the door, but growth is often slow. Some struggles have deep roots and will take time, patience, and wise help to heal. That is normal. It is not a sign that God has given up on you. "There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus" (Romans 8:1). You are not a lost cause. Keep coming back to the Father, keep using the RUN plan, and let other believers walk with you.

blocks.title: If you have been harmed
content: If someone used their power to pressure or harm you sexually, what was done to you is not your sin to confess. It was sin against you. Please tell a pastor, a counselor, or another safe and trusted person, and let them help you get care.
If a child is being harmed, contact local authorities right away. If you are in immediate danger, call 911.

blocks.text: 9.4 - Who is one mature, trusted believer you could ask to pray for you and check in with you about purity? What would help you take that step? You do not need to write any private details here.
Lesson 9 Review

David did not run. His fall began when he pursued what he saw, and it grew in hiding. His restoration began when he stopped hiding and confessed, and God forgave him. Purity is not how you earn God's love. It is how you protect a heart that already belongs to Him. When temptation fires the starting gun, RUN: Remember the Cross, remember you are United with God, and remember you Need others. In the next lesson, you will come to the table Jesus set for His people, where that same grace is put on display.
